items.title: The Essential-Body Verses Open: Avoid All Evil, Abandon All Desire

items.zh: 「常樂居遠離，及邊際臥具，恒修習善法，堅精進勇猛」者，此頌顯示若身若心皆遠離故；習近順定諸臥具故；遠離一切不善尋思，純修白淨諸善法故；非沈掉等諸隨煩惱所摧蔽故；能善圓滿正加行故；增上心學方便殊勝。「無有欲、生欲，不憎惡、憎惡，離睡眠、睡眠，時不居寂靜，離惡作、惡作，無希慮、希慮；一切種恒時，成就正方便」者，此二頌中，顯示遠離貪欲、瞋恚、惛沈睡眠、掉舉惡作，及疑蓋故；於諸善法生起欲故；於諸欲中極憎厭故；為修善品方便加行有所堪任，及心安靜，於時時間習睡眠故；若心沈沒或慮彼生，於淨妙相思惟作意，及遊行時不居靜故；於先所犯，便生憂悔，於所不犯無憂悔故；後後殊勝生希慮故；殷重、無間正方便故；增上心學轉得清淨。「引發、與覺悟、及和合所結、有相、若親昵、亦多種喜樂、侵逼、極親昵，名虛妄分別；能生於欲貪，智者當遠離」者，此二頌中，顯示八種虛妄分別，能生婬欲所有貪愛。從初方便次第生起，乃至究竟。由遠離故，諸所修學清淨殊勝。引發分別者，謂能引發於可愛事、不正思惟相應之心所有分別。覺悟分別者，謂即於彼可愛事中，覺悟貪纏相應分別。和合所結分別者，謂即於彼可愛事中所有分別。有相分別者，謂即於彼可愛事中，執取種種淨妙相狀所有分別。親昵分別者，謂於已得所愛事中，勇勵相應所有分別。喜樂分別者，謂即於彼所得事中，種種受用悕慕愛樂種種門轉所有分別。侵逼分別者，謂兩根會時所有分別。極親昵分別者，謂不淨出時所有分別。「諸欲、令無飽，眾多所共有，是非法因緣，能增長貪愛，賢聖所應離，速趣於壞滅，仗託於眾緣，危逸所依地」者，此二頌中，顯示八種現法後法如其所應諸欲過患。若能觀見，即是斷除欲愛方便。「諸欲、如枯骨，亦如軟肉段，如草炬相似，猶如大火坑。譬如蟒毒蛇，亦如夢所見，如借莊嚴具，如樹端熟果。如是知諸欲，都不應耽樂」者，此中廣引如前所說令無飽等，於諸欲中八種過患，一切世間共成譬喻，顯示諸欲過患深重。又為顯示於諸欲中具有如是眾多過患，分明可了，何有智者於彼耽樂。又彼諸欲如枯骨故，令無飽滿；如段肉故，眾多共有；猶如草炬，正起現前極燒惱故，非法因緣；如大火坑，生渴愛故，增長貪愛；如蟒毒故，賢聖遠離；如夢見故，速趣壞滅；猶如假借莊嚴具故，仗託眾緣；猶如樹端爛熟果故，危亡放逸所依之地。「當聽聞正法，常思惟、修習，先觀見麁靜，次於修一向，捨煩惱麁重，於斷生欣樂，於諸相觀察，得加行究竟，能離欲界欲，及離色界欲，入真諦現觀，能離一切欲，證現法涅槃，及餘依永盡」者，此中顯示由了相等七種作意，世出世道皆清淨故；證得有餘及無餘依二涅槃果，增上慧學究竟清淨。聽聞正法，常思惟言，顯示了相作意。常修習言，顯示勝解作意。由起勝解而修習故。先觀見麁靜言，顯示遠離作意。於修習一向等言，顯示攝樂作意。於諸相觀察言，顯示觀察作意。加行究竟言，顯示加行究竟作意。能離欲界欲，及離色界欲，入真諦現觀，能離一切欲等言，顯示世間、出世間加行究竟果作意。
items.en: 'Always delight in dwelling in seclusion, and in remote lodgings; constantly cultivate wholesome dharmas, with firm effort and courage': this verse shows that the means of the training in higher mind is excellent, because one is secluded in both body and mind; because one keeps to lodgings that favour concentration; because one leaves behind all unwholesome thoughts and cultivates only pure wholesome dharmas; because one is not overcome by secondary afflictions such as sinking and excitement; and because one can fully complete right application. 'Without desire, yet generating desire; without aversion, yet having aversion; free from sleep, yet sleeping; at times not dwelling in quiet; free from regret, yet regretting; without longing, yet longing; in every way and at all times, accomplishing right means': these two verses show that the training in higher mind becomes ever purer because one leaves behind the hindrances of sensual desire, ill will, lethargy and drowsiness, restlessness and regret, and doubt; because one generates desire for wholesome dharmas; because one is deeply averse to sense pleasures; because, so as to be fit for the application of cultivating wholesome qualities and to keep the mind calm, one sleeps at the proper times; because, when the mind sinks or one fears it may, one attends to a pure and beautiful sign, and when walking about one does not stay in quiet; because one feels regret for offences committed before, and no regret for what one has not committed; because one longs for ever higher attainment; and because one's right means are earnest and uninterrupted. 'Drawing forth, awakening, binding through union, having signs, intimacy, many kinds of delight, pressing, and extreme intimacy: these are called false discriminations; they produce sensual lust, and the wise should leave them behind': these two verses show the eight kinds of false discrimination that produce craving for sexual desire, arising in order from the first preparation to its completion. By leaving them behind, all that is trained becomes pure and excellent. 'Drawing-forth discrimination' is the discrimination of a mind associated with incorrect reflection that draws forth an attractive object. 'Awakening discrimination' is the discrimination, associated with the entanglement of greed, that awakens to that attractive object. 'Discrimination bound through union' is the discrimination concerning that attractive object. 'Discrimination having signs' is the discrimination that grasps the various pure and beautiful features of that attractive object. 'Intimacy discrimination' is the discrimination associated with eagerness towards the beloved object once obtained. 'Delight discrimination' is the discrimination that proceeds in various ways, longing for and delighting in the many ways of enjoying what has been obtained. 'Pressing discrimination' is the discrimination at the time the two organs meet. 'Extreme-intimacy discrimination' is the discrimination at the time the impure fluid is emitted. 'Sense pleasures are never satisfying, shared by many, a cause of what is not Dharma; they increase craving, should be left behind by the wise and noble, quickly go to ruin, rely on many conditions, and are the ground of danger and heedlessness': these two verses show eight dangers of sense pleasures, in this life and the next, as appropriate. Seeing them is the means of cutting off desire for sense pleasures. 'Sense pleasures are like a dry bone, like a piece of soft flesh, like a grass torch, like a great pit of fire, like a venomous snake, like what is seen in a dream, like borrowed ornaments, like ripe fruit at the top of a tree. Knowing sense pleasures in this way, one should not delight in them at all': here, for the eight dangers in sense pleasures stated above, such as never being satisfying, similes accepted by the whole world are cited at length to show how deep and heavy the dangers of sense pleasures are. It also shows that, since sense pleasures so clearly have these many dangers, what wise person would delight in them? Further, sense pleasures are never satisfying, as a dry bone is; shared by many, as a piece of flesh is; a cause of what is not Dharma, as a grass torch is, because it burns fiercely the moment it is lit; they increase craving, as a great pit of fire does, because they produce thirst; the wise and noble leave them behind, as they would venom; they quickly go to ruin, as what is seen in a dream does; they rely on many conditions, as borrowed ornaments do; they are the ground of danger, ruin, and heedlessness, as over-ripe fruit at the top of a tree is. 'One should listen to the true Dharma and always reflect and cultivate; first see the coarse and the calm, then cultivate single-mindedly; give up the coarse burden of the afflictions and delight in abandonment; examine the signs, reach the completion of application; leave behind the desire of the desire realm and the desire of the form realm; enter the direct realisation of the truths, leave behind all desire, realise nirvana in this present life, and the final exhaustion of the remainder': this shows that, through the seven attentions beginning with the attention that discerns characteristics, both the worldly and world-transcending paths are purified; one realises the two fruits of nirvana, with remainder and without remainder, and the training in higher wisdom is ultimately purified. The words 'listen to the true Dharma and always reflect' show the attention that discerns characteristics. 'Always cultivate' shows the attention of conviction, because one cultivates by generating conviction. 'First see the coarse and the calm' shows the attention of seclusion. 'Cultivate single-mindedly' and so on shows the attention that gathers joy. 'Examine the signs' shows the attention of examination. 'Completion of application' shows the attention of completing application. The words 'leave behind the desire of the desire realm and the desire of the form realm; enter the direct realisation of the truths; leave behind all desire', and so on, show the attention of the fruit of completing application, worldly and world-transcending.

blocks.text: The last part of the prose on the three trainings. **Again none of today's Chinese is in Ru-Yi's translation.** It explains the verses on concentration and wisdom you read on Day 133. Tomorrow we return to Ru-Yi's English.

items: **The means of higher mind.** Delight in solitude means withdrawal of both body and mind; simple bedding suits concentration; one abandons unwholesome thoughts, is not overwhelmed by dullness and agitation, and perfects right effort.

**The five hindrances in pairs.** The two verses "without desire, yet with desire; without aversion, yet with aversion…" show freedom from the hindrances of sensual desire, ill will, dullness and sleep, agitation and remorse, and doubt, while keeping their wholesome counterparts: desire for good things, aversion towards sense pleasures, sleep at proper times, remorse only for real faults, and aspiration for ever higher attainment.

**Eight false conceptions.** Lust develops in eight stages of conceptual construction, from the first improper thought about an attractive object, through awakening of craving, fixation on its features, effort to obtain, delight in enjoyment, to sexual union and its culmination. The wise keep far from all of them.

**Eight faults of desire.** Desires never satisfy; are shared by many; are causes of wrongdoing; increase craving; are shunned by the noble; quickly perish; depend on many conditions; and are the ground of danger and heedlessness.

**Eight similes.** The prose pairs them in order: like a dry bone, never satisfying; like a piece of meat, shared by many; like a grass torch, burning; like a fire pit, increasing thirst; like a venomous snake, shunned by the noble; like a dream, soon gone; like borrowed ornaments, dependent on conditions; like ripe fruit at the top of a tree, a place of danger. Master Cháng Bǎi's reading on Day 133 follows exactly this pairing.

**Seven attentions.** The last verse maps onto the seven attentions (Day 108): hearing and reflecting is the attention discerning characteristics; cultivating is resolve; seeing the coarse and the calm is seclusion; single-minded practice is gathering joy; examining marks is investigation; culmination of effort is final application; freedom from the desires of each realm and entry into the truths is its result. Through these, the mundane and supramundane paths are purified, and one attains nirvāṇa with and without remainder.

subs.head: Why the commentary is so detailed here

blocks.text: The description of the eight conceptions is frank, written for monastics who must understand exactly how lust takes hold in order to stop it early. The lesson for any reader is that a strong craving does not arrive all at once. It grows by stages, and the earlier one sees it, the easier it is to let go.

quiz.q: How does the prose read the paired phrase "without desire, yet with desire" (無有欲、生欲)?
options: It is a paradox with no meaning
Free of the hindrance of sensual desire, yet generating desire for wholesome things
Desire comes and goes at random
Desire is neither good nor bad
quiz.why: The prose explains that one is free of the hindrance of sensual desire while generating wholesome desire (於諸善法生起欲).

quiz.q: In the prose, which fault of desire is paired with the simile "like a grass torch"?
options: Being a cause of wrongdoing, because it burns as soon as it is taken up
quiz.why: "Like a grass torch, burning fiercely as it is raised, hence a cause of wrongdoing" (猶如草炬，正起現前極燒惱故，非法因緣).

quiz.q: Which attention does the prose link to "first observe the coarse and the still"?
quiz.why: 先觀見麁靜言，顯示遠離作意: seeing the coarse and the calm shows the attention of seclusion.
